Forest Village Rules

Forest animals build a village through one year, from spring to winter. Whoever has the most points after winter wins; alone you play for a target score.

The rules

Resources and the forest
There are three resources: clay, seeds and feathers. The forest has eight fields: Clay Bank (2 clay), Seed Patch (2 seeds), Feather Nest (2 feathers), Fern Path (1 clay and 1 feather), Moss Trail (1 seed and 1 feather), Sunny Hollow (1 clay and 1 seed), Old Oak (1 clay and 1 card) and Market (2 cards). Every field takes any number of squirrels. The first squirrel on a field in a season also gets its extra: 1 more of the field's resource, 1 card, or at the Old Oak 1 feather.
A turn
On your turn, first send one of your free squirrels to a field and take what it gives. Then you may build one card, or end your turn. If you cannot pay for any card, your turn ends at once. Then the next player who still has a free squirrel is on.
Buildings and animals
Build cards from your hand or from the Clearing, where 6 cards are open; a taken card is replaced at once. Every card belongs to one of five habitats: stream, hedge, rock, treetop and heath. An animal costs one feather less while its habitat has more buildings than animals in your village. Cards give resources or cards once when built; production cards give their goods when built and again after every second squirrel you send. A village holds at most 12 cards; there is no hand limit.
Seasons
Everybody plays the same season. In spring each player has 3 squirrels; at the start of every later season you get one more squirrel for every 4 cards in your village (at most 6). When all squirrels are out, the season ends: the squirrels come back, every hand is filled up to 4 cards, and the next player in turn starts the new season. Everybody also starts the game with 4 cards; the second seat starts with 1 feather, the third with 1 clay and 1 feather, the fourth with 1 of each resource.
End and points
The game ends after winter. Points come from the cards in your village, 3 points for every home range (a habitat with at least 3 cards in your village), the end bonuses of some cards and the task card: one task lies open each game, and everyone who fulfils it at the end gets its points.
Alone
With 1 player you play the same rules and win if you have at least 45 points at the end.
Playing
Tap a field of the forest to send a squirrel there; fields that still have their extra show it. Then tap a card in your hand or in the Clearing to read it, and Build or End turn; cards you cannot pay for now say so. The list below shows the last moves, including the computer's. Against the computer: Easy often plays at random, Medium builds what looks best now, Hard also looks ahead to the next card, the home ranges and the end. On one device the hand is covered between turns.

Example

You pay 2 clay and 1 feather for the Bakery, a hedge building. It gives you 2 feathers when built and again after every second squirrel you send. Then the Hedgehog – or any other hedge animal – costs one feather less. With a third hedge card you have a home range worth 3 points.
